ap_calculus_bc-m01.stem: The first four terms $a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4$ of a geometric series are shown in the graph, where the points are joined by line segments. What is the sum of the infinite geometric series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n$?

stimulus.description: Graph of the terms a_n for n = 1 to 4, joined by line segments.

options.why: The ratio is r = a2/a1 = \frac{2}{3} and the series converges since |r| < 1, so the sum is a1/(1 - r).
Starts the sum at the second term: a2/(1 - r).
Adds only the four terms shown instead of all infinitely many terms.

blueprint.subject: ap_calculus_bc
blueprint.concept: Find the sum of a geometric series whose first terms are read from a graph
student_thinking: Read a1 and a2 from the graph and compute the common ratio
Check |r| < 1 so that the series converges

key_conditions.condition: the terms have a constant ratio and |r| < 1
key_conditions.evidence: the plotted terms decrease by a constant factor

verification.independent_path: partial sum of 400 terms computed in floating point (independent of the closed form)

ap_calculus_bc-m02.stem: The population $P(t)$ of a species satisfies a logistic differential equation. The graph of $P$ and the horizontal line it approaches (dashed) are shown. For what value of $P$ is the population growing fastest?

stimulus.description: Graph of the logistic population P(t) with its horizontal asymptote drawn dashed.

options.why: Reports the initial population P(0), where growth is slow.
For a logistic model dP/dt is largest when P is half the carrying capacity, which is the value of the dashed line divided by 2.
Takes one quarter of the carrying capacity.
Reports the carrying capacity K, the limiting value, instead of the population when growth is fastest.

blueprint.subject: ap_calculus_bc
blueprint.concept: Use the carrying capacity read from a graph to find the population at which logistic growth is fastest
student_thinking: Read the carrying capacity from the dashed horizontal line
Recall that dP/dt = k P (1 - P/K) is greatest at P = K/2
Compute half of the carrying capacity

key_conditions.condition: the model is logistic so the horizontal asymptote is the carrying capacity K

must_include: dashed horizontal line at the carrying capacity

verification.independent_path: finite-difference growth rate of the plotted curve is largest near P = K/2 (independent of the logistic formula)

ap_calculus_bc-m03.stem: A particle moves in the $xy$-plane with position $(x(t),y(t))$. The graphs of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ for $0\le t\le 8$ are shown, and each consists of line segments. During which of the following time intervals is the particle at rest?

stimulus.description: Graphs of x(t) and y(t), each consisting of line segments connecting the plotted vertices.

options.why: Only y is constant on (4, 6); x is changing, so the particle is moving horizontally.
On this interval both graphs are horizontal, so x' = 0 and y' = 0 and the speed is zero.
Only x is constant on (0, 2); y is changing, so the particle is moving vertically.
Both x and y are changing on (6, 8), so the particle is moving.

blueprint.subject: ap_calculus_bc
blueprint.concept: Decide when a particle with parametric position is at rest from the slopes of both position graphs
student_thinking: The particle is at rest when x' = 0 and y' = 0 at the same time
Compare the slope of the graph of x and of y on each interval
Select the interval where both slopes are zero

key_conditions.condition: speed is sqrt((x')^2 + (y')^2) and is zero only when both derivatives are zero
key_conditions.evidence: definition of speed for planar motion

verification.independent_path: numerical speed from central differences of both interpolated graphs at each interval midpoint (independent of the slope comparison)
